version.changelog: Security fix: patch shell injection vulnerability. --open flag and df disk check now use spawn/spawnSync with array args (no shell). All execSync calls are hardcoded strings with zero variable interpolation.

llm.summary: The skill mostly matches its stated local dashboard purpose, but it needs review because private usage metadata can be exposed through unauthenticated dashboard APIs and there is a verified browser security flaw.

dimensions.detail: Default binding is loopback, but server.js accepts arbitrary --host values while the APIs have no authentication; dashboard.html also builds inline event handlers from log-derived identifiers, creating a stored DOM XSS risk in the dashboard origin.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The artifact uses a zero-dependency Node.js server and static HTML with no package installation, remote payload retrieval, or install-time persistence found.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The trigger phrases include broad requests such as system health, token usage, and how many requests, which may cause a local server and log reading workflow when the user expected a simpler answer.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No durable service, scheduled task, filesystem write, or privilege escalation was found; the server runs until stopped and the page stores only display color preferences in browser localStorage.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The skill coherently provides an OpenClaw usage dashboard by reading local session logs, model configuration metadata, and system health data; those capabilities align with the stated purpose but involve private local telemetry.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review before installing, especially on shared or networked machines. Use only the default localhost binding, do not run it with --host 0.0.0.0 or another non-loopback address, and treat the dashboard as exposing private OpenClaw usage patterns, model choices, agent names, session timing, and system details.
llm.findings:
[P2] expected: Downgraded: the cited hidden-instruction evidence is an ordinary HTML comment labeling the timeline section, not an agent-directed instruction or prompt override.
[LP3] expected: Partly accepted: local file reading and a localhost server are purpose-aligned and disclosed, but the skill metadata does not clearly scope or gate those capabilities.
[SQP-1] unexpected: Accepted as a review concern: broad triggers could invoke log reading and dashboard startup for ambiguous requests.
[SQP-2] expected: Mostly purpose-aligned: the SKILL and README disclose local session-log reading and localhost display, though users should understand that the dashboard exposes private usage metadata locally.
[SDI-1] expected: Downgraded: showing configured model information fits the dashboard's stated model-activity purpose, but it broadens the local metadata shown to anyone who can access the dashboard.
[T09] unexpected: Accepted: dashboard.html uses innerHTML with inline onclick/onkeydown handlers containing log-derived model or agent identifiers; HTML escaping alone is not safe for that nested JavaScript context while unsafe-inline is allowed.
[T09] unexpected: Accepted: server.js defaults to 127.0.0.1, but an arbitrary --host value can expose unauthenticated /api/stats, /api/system, and /api/config responses beyond localhost, conflicting with the localhost-only framing.
